Q203301: Capital of Abia State in southeastern Nigeria, on the Port Harcourt–Enugu railway.
Served as the capital of Biafra for much of the Nigerian Civil War, after Enugu fell.
An agricultural market town; the National Root Crops Research Institute is nearby at Umudike.
Q1636: Capital of Rizal province, on the hills east of Metro Manila.
A pilgrimage city: the Antipolo Cathedral shrine of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage draws crowds every May.
Known for suman (sticky-rice snacks), cashews and views over Manila at night.
Q210365: Port city in southern Guangxi on the Gulf of Tonkin; formerly Pakhoi.
One of the starting points of the ancient Maritime Silk Road (Hepu).
Famous for Silver Beach and its 'Hepu pearls'.
Weizhou Island, a young volcanic island, belongs to it.
Q71339: City in Hubei northwest of Wuhan; the name means 'filial piety moves (heaven)'.
Named after the legend of Dong Yong, who sold himself to pay for his father's funeral.
Known for its rice-wine (mijiu) and sesame candy.
Q738303: The largest city of Tamaulipas, on the Rio Grande opposite Hidalgo and McAllen, Texas.
One of the busiest border crossings for trade.
Q888794: Town in Fars province, about 80 km east of Shiraz.
Lies near Lake Bakhtegan and Lake Tashk, important wetlands for flamingos.
Q92348: City in southeastern Jilin bordering North Korea; the name means 'White Mountain'.
Named after Changbai Mountain (Paektu), with its crater lake Heaven Lake.
Known for mineral water springs and ginseng.
Q1015823: County-level city on the Yangtze under Wuxi, one of China's richest county-level cities.
Home of many large private companies, like Sunshine Group and Haixin.
Hometown of the Ming travel writer Xu Xiake.
Q216847: City in Colombia on the border with Venezuela.
Birthplace of Francisco de Paula Santander, a founder of Colombia.
The 1821 Congress of Cúcuta wrote the constitution of Gran Colombia.
A key crossing for trade and for migrants from Venezuela.
Q1918837: City in northern Bangladesh on the Karatoya River.
Mahasthangarh nearby is the oldest known city site in Bangladesh (3rd century BC).
Famous for its sweet yoghurt (Bogurar doi).
Named after Nasiruddin Bughra Khan, a 13th-century governor of Bengal.
Q173270: Mexico's oldest and most important port, on the Gulf of Mexico.
Founded by Hernán Cortés in 1519 at the start of the conquest of the Aztecs.
Called 'Heroic Veracruz' for resisting invasions by France and the USA.
Famous for son jarocho music and its café culture.
Q2051: Jambi is the capital of Jambi province on the Batang Hari River in Sumatra.
Near the Muaro Jambi temple complex, one of the largest ancient Buddhist sites in Southeast Asia.
Was part of the Malayu and Srivijaya kingdoms; today a centre of rubber and palm oil.
Q11026: Port city on the north coast of Central Java, called the 'City of Batik'.
Its batik shows Chinese, Arab, Dutch and Javanese influences in bright colours.
The first Southeast Asian city in UNESCO's Creative Cities Network (2014); has a Batik Museum.
Q34804: The largest city in New Mexico, on the Rio Grande below the Sandia Mountains.
Founded in 1706 as a Spanish outpost on the Camino Real.
Hosts the world's largest hot-air balloon festival every October.
Setting of the TV series 'Breaking Bad'.
Q427367: City in eastern Sichuan near Chongqing.
Birthplace of Deng Xiaoping, China's leader who started the reforms of 1978; his home is a museum.
Q462789: City on Florida's Gulf Coast in the Fort Myers area.
Has over 640 km of canals, more than any other city in the world.
Founded in 1957 as a planned community; known for burrowing owls.
Q170616: Capital of Chiba Prefecture on Tokyo Bay, east of Tokyo.
Its Makuhari district hosts the Makuhari Messe convention centre (Tokyo Game Show).
Has the world's longest suspended monorail.
Near Narita International Airport and Tokyo Disneyland in the prefecture.
Q1365723: Provincial capital just north of Bangkok, part of its metropolitan area.
Home to Thammasat University's Rangsit campus and big industrial estates.
Its name means 'city of lotuses'; founded by Mon settlers.
Q621001: Capital of Malanje Province in northern Angola, 380 km east of Luanda.
Near the Kalandula Falls, among the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume.
Also near the black rocks of Pungo Andongo and the habitat of the rare giant sable antelope.
Q49174: The most populous city in Connecticut, on Long Island Sound.
P. T. Barnum, the circus showman, was its mayor and lived here; the Barnum Museum is in the city.
Part of the New York metropolitan area with Stamford and Norwalk.
Q210886: Capital of Tabasco in southeast Mexico; the name means 'beautiful town'.
Centre of Mexico's oil industry ('Energy City of Mexico').
The Parque-Museo La Venta has giant Olmec stone heads.
Q318156: City in Punjab, Pakistan, at the edge of the Cholistan Desert.
Capital of the princely state of Bahawalpur, ruled by Nawabs until 1955.
Known for its palaces, like Noor Mahal, and the Derawar Fort in the desert.
Gateway to Lal Suhanra National Park.
Q152831: City in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq near the Turkish border.
Capital of Duhok Governorate, in a valley of the Zagros foothills.
Hosted many refugee camps for Yazidis and Syrians after 2014; the Duhok Dam is nearby.
Q1197949: Known as a 'hometown of Chinese cuisine' (Lu cuisine).
Was mentioned in the Jackie Chan film 'Police Story 3'.
Q1990163: River-port city southeast of Dhaka on the Shitalakshya River.
Called the 'Dundee of Bangladesh' for its jute mills.
Today a centre of knitwear and garment factories.
Nearby Sonargaon was the medieval capital of Bengal.
Q7567412: The conurbation of Portsmouth and Southampton on England's south coast, sometimes called 'Solent City'.
Portsmouth is the home of the Royal Navy with HMS Victory; Southampton is a major cruise port.
The Titanic sailed from Southampton in 1912.
Includes Gosport, Fareham, Havant and Eastleigh.
Q2222874: Main city of Zanzibar island in Tanzania.
Its Stone Town, with Swahili, Arab, Indian and European buildings and carved doors, is a World Heritage Site.
Was the capital of the Sultanate of Zanzibar and a centre of the spice and slave trade.
Q2761728: City in northern Karnataka, twin city of Hubballi.
An education centre with Karnatak University and an agricultural university.
Famous for Hindustani music (Gangubai Hangal, Bhimsen Joshi) and the Dharwad pedha sweet.
Q3120966: City in Andhra Pradesh near the new capital region of Amaravati.
The world's largest chilli trading market is here.
Also a big centre of cotton and tobacco trade.
Q7986320: The western part of the Witwatersrand, west of Johannesburg.
Settled after gold was found in 1886; includes Krugersdorp, Randfontein and Roodepoort.
Near the Cradle of Humankind fossil sites (World Heritage Site).
Q33959: City on the French Riviera, at the foot of the Alps near Monaco and Italy.
Belonged to Savoy/Sardinia until it became French in 1860.
Famous for the Promenade des Anglais and the Carnival of Nice; Matisse and Chagall museums are here.
With Cannes, home of the film festival, it forms the Côte d'Azur urban area.
Q875070: City on Lingayen Gulf in Pangasinan, Philippines.
Famous for bangus (milkfish), celebrated with a yearly Bangus Festival.
Badly hit by the 1990 Luzon earthquake.
Q842411: Twin city of Ayodhya on the Saryu River, Uttar Pradesh.
The first capital of the Nawabs of Awadh, with the tomb of Bahu Begum and the Gulab Bari garden.
Next to Ayodhya, the birthplace of Rama and site of the new Ram temple (2024).
Q1136189: City in northern Bihar, the cultural centre of the Mithila region.
Seat of the Darbhanga Raj, once one of India's richest zamindari estates.
Known for Madhubani (Mithila) painting, makhana (fox nuts) and Maithili culture.
Q214173: Peru's third city, on the northern coast.
Near Chan Chan, the largest adobe city in the world, capital of the Chimú (World Heritage Site).
The Moche Huacas of the Sun and Moon are nearby.
Known as the 'City of Eternal Spring' and the home of the marinera dance.
Q1006338: Headquarters of Nadia district, West Bengal.
Famous for its clay dolls (ghurni) and the sweet sarpuria.
Named after Raja Krishnachandra Roy, an 18th-century ruler and patron of the arts.
Q75110: The largest Chinese border city, on the Yalu River opposite Sinuiju, North Korea.
Most of China's trade with North Korea passes over its Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge.
The 'Broken Bridge' was bombed by the US in the Korean War; the Great Wall's eastern end (Hushan) is nearby.
Q492552: Uzbekistan's third city, at the northern edge of the Fergana Valley.
A historic craft and trade centre since the 17th century.
Famous for flowers and its yearly flower festival.
Q466046: City opposite Rabat on the Bou Regreg river.
In the 17th century it was a pirate republic whose corsairs raided as far as Iceland.
Its walled medina has Marinid monuments like the Great Mosque.
Connected to Rabat by a tram over the river.
Q75379: Coastal city in western Liaoning; the name means 'gourd island'.
Includes Xingcheng, a well-preserved Ming walled town.
Q189138: Capital of Sonora in northwest Mexico.
A car-manufacturing centre with a large Ford plant.
Known for carne asada, flour tortillas and the Cerro de la Campana hill.
One of the hottest cities in Mexico.
Q645725: City in the Mumbai metropolitan region, northeast of Thane.
Once called the 'Manchester of India' for its power-loom textile industry.
Today one of India's biggest warehouse and logistics hubs.
Q42108: City in Gyeonggi Province south of Seoul.
Its Bundang and Pangyo districts are planned new towns; Pangyo Techno Valley is called Korea's Silicon Valley.
Headquarters of Naver, Kakao and many game companies.
Q168929: Capital of Mato Grosso do Sul in central-west Brazil.
A planned city with wide, tree-lined avenues; called the 'Brunette City' for its red soil.
Gateway to the Pantanal wetlands and Bonito.
Has large Japanese (Okinawan) and Paraguayan communities — known for sobá noodles.
Q192387: The second city of Paraná in southern Brazil.
Founded in 1930 by a British company; the name means 'little London'.
Grew rich with coffee farming; has a large Japanese-Brazilian community.
Home of the State University of Londrina.
Q1452991: City near Agra in Uttar Pradesh.
The centre of India's glass industry, especially glass bangles.
Named after Firoz Shah, an officer of the Mughal emperor Akbar.
Q34692: Capital of Jamaica, on a natural harbour on the southeast coast.
Founded in 1692 after an earthquake destroyed nearby Port Royal, the 'wickedest city on Earth'.
Birthplace of reggae, ska and dancehall; the Bob Marley Museum is here.
The largest English-speaking city south of the US in the Americas.
Q1142677: The municipality of Hermosillo, the largest in Sonora state.
Includes the coastal town Bahía Kino on the Gulf of California.
Its seat is the state capital Hermosillo.
Q837425: Second city of Xinjiang, seat of Bayingolin Mongol Prefecture, China's largest prefecture.
A base of the Tarim Basin oil fields; Bosten Lake is nearby.
Q44059: Capital of Buenos Aires Province, built from 1882 as a planned city.
Laid out in a square grid with diagonal avenues; called the 'City of Diagonals'.
Its neo-Gothic cathedral and the Natural Science Museum are landmarks.
Was named 'Ciudad Eva Perón' from 1952 to 1955.
Q5753: Uzbekistan's second city, one of the oldest cities of Central Asia.
A great Silk Road city; conquered by Alexander the Great (as Maracanda).
Timur (Tamerlane) made it his capital; the Registan square with three madrasas is a World Heritage Site.
Also has Timur's tomb Gur-e-Amir and the Bibi-Khanym Mosque.
Q75203: City in Liaoning on the Taizi River, south of Shenyang.
One of the oldest cities in Northeast China; Nurhaci's Later Jin made it a capital (1621–1625).
Its White Pagoda (Liao dynasty) is one of the tallest brick pagodas in the northeast.
Q48256: Ukraine's fourth city, on the Dnieper River.
Founded as Yekaterinoslav by Catherine the Great; called Dnipropetrovsk from 1926 to 2016.
A centre of the Soviet missile and space industry (Yuzhmash).
Has one of the longest river promenades in Europe and the Menorah Jewish community centre.
Q994085: Capital of Kogi State, at the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers.
Founded in 1857 by the explorer William Balfour Baikie as a trading post.
Was the first administrative capital of the British Northern Nigeria Protectorate; Lord Lugard's house survives.
The name 'Nigeria' was coined by Flora Shaw, Lugard's wife.
Q888665: Municipality in Alappuzha district, Kerala, south of Kochi.
Lies in the coir and backwater region of Kerala.
Known for the Cherthala Karthyayani temple.
Q14182: The largest city of South Kalimantan, on the Barito and Martapura rivers.
Called the 'City of a Thousand Rivers'.
Famous for its floating markets, like Lok Baintan.
Q58235: City in western Zhejiang on the upper Qiantang River.
Home of the southern branch of the Confucius family temple (Nanzong Kong temple).
Mount Jianglang, with three giant rock peaks, is a World Heritage Site.
Known for spicy rabbit heads and duck heads.
Q1880: Chile's second-largest urban area, at the mouth of the Biobío River.
Founded in 1550 by Pedro de Valdivia; moved after earthquakes and tsunamis.
Hit by the 1960 Valdivia earthquake (the strongest ever recorded) and the 2010 earthquake.
A big university and industrial centre; residents are called penquistas.
Q85751443: Administrative centre of Chandanaish Upazila, south of Chittagong.
Q73073: The southernmost city of Shanxi, near the Yellow River bend.
Built around the Yuncheng Salt Lake, which has supplied salt for over 4,000 years.
Hometown of Guan Yu, the Three Kingdoms general worshipped as a god; the Guandi Temple at Xiezhou is the largest of its kind.
The Stork Tower (Guanque Lou), famous in Tang poetry, is in the prefecture.
